data.long_meaning: The name Birju is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Bir', which means 'Bold, Brave, Heroic'. In Hindu mythology, Birju is an epithet for Lord Krishna, who is known for his bravery and heroic deeds. The name Birju carries the meaning “Bold, Brave, Heroic” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Birju usually hope their child will grow to embody bold, brave, heroic and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.context: A military alliance of Hindu Rajputs and Jats led by Raja BirSingh Rajput of Amber, Rajasthan. The name 'Birju Sena' translates to 'Army of Heroes'. The alliance was formed to counter the Mughal invasion of North India, and BirSingh successfully resisted the Mughals with the help of his army. Despite their military successes, the Rajputs and Jats of Birju Sena were eventually defeated by the Mughals in the Battle of Haldighati in 1576.
